title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll dealt a hand from the catalog; the strongest challenger — the one-bit desktop — takes the build. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.lineage: early one-bit desktop computers, ordered dithers, marching ants
options.thesis: The board as a ditherpunk operating system: every gray is a stipple, every window is a column, every drag is marching ants.
options.viewport: A dithered desktop where columns tile edge-to-edge as windows with title bars; cards are file rectangles whose selection wears marching ants; the archive is a trash can whose lid pops pixel by pixel.
options.risk: Small body type at strict bitmap sizes is the legibility cliff; premium lives entirely in dither craft, and weak dithers read as cheap.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.lineage: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Each column is one luminous gauge owning one truth; the cross-check sweep is the reading order.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: states map to needle position, Done is the green arc with the lamp out. Loses the build on identification — the pilot's deck is adjacent to this audience's world, not inside it — and its fixed six-gauge grammar fights boards with more columns than six.
options.viewport: A matte black panel: columns as round dials with placard caps, cards as needle readings with damped spring motion, Done a needle seated in the green arc with its lamp out.
options.risk: The six-pack constellation is fixed while kanban columns are not; over-lit, it becomes a cockpit toy.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.lineage: orienteering map and legend, iso-standard terrain inks
options.thesis: The board is terrain with a fixed color language; cards are the purple course riding over it, control to control.
options.case: Fuses well: columns as terrain zones, cards as numbered controls, Done as punched controls. Loses the build on clarity — the terrain language is fixed and standard while the product's labels are user-owned colors, and a board that changes its map colors on demand breaks the grammar.
options.viewport: A fixed-scale terrain map in iso inks with the purple course line riding above: each column a zone, each card a control circle with its number, Done a punched card.
options.risk: The terrain grammar is strict and standard; letting users tint columns breaks the language, and the metaphor reads oblique to non-orienteers.

options.label: Drafting Room
options.lineage: the blue-line technical drawing studio: drafting film, stencils, title blocks
options.thesis: The board is a drafting table; columns are pinned sheets with title blocks, cards are stenciled components with dimension callouts, and Done is an approval stamp.
options.case: The roll's own grounded direction. Loses the build narrowly on audience identification — the drafting table is the designer's world, one step removed from the developer's — while matching it on clarity.
options.viewport: A sheet of drafting film: columns as pinned drawing sheets with title blocks and revision lines, cards as stenciled components with leaders and callouts, In Progress under a highlighter sweep, Done stamped APPROVED in rotated red.
options.risk: A quiet, technical register that reads cold if the stamps and ruled texture are not carried at full commitment.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: a soft-surface kanban with rounded columns and one accent, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects — three rounded columns on a soft ground — at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Safe by design; it is the door, not the destination.
